limitations: Initial CreateStream response was empty and JSON decoding failed before its HTTP status was retained; no AWS rejection is inferred. The following DescribeStreamSummary calls establish the owned stream exists. Subsequent empty responses preserve the exact empty body.

Single account, us-east-1, one one-shard provisioned stream and one short-lived registered consumer. Other regions, modes, resharding, encryption, throughput errors and retention/iterator-expiry timing were not tested.

One operation-specific valid payload plus bounded malformed/missing payload samples is not exhaustive validation coverage. In particular, DryRunOperationException does not imply all ordinary semantic checks occurred, as the paired native controls show.

No successful ordinary SubscribeToShard event-stream session was opened in this capture. Consumer metadata and repeated DryRun responses cannot establish active subscription-slot, heartbeat or delivery-metric behavior.

CloudWatch sampled only the listed AWS/Kinesis stream-dimension metrics with Period=60 and Sum, without waiting for eventual publication. Empty datapoints do not prove no emission; zero sums are actual metric datapoints. CLI metric timestamps retain the native CLI timezone offset. The two real control writes occurred in a later minute than the queried EndTime.

The early GetRecords/SubscribeToShard dry-run-only metric window also contains invalid and denied DryRun requests and normal setup calls. It is not a request-isolated billing or request-count experiment. No billing claim is made.

No stress, retention waits, paid commitments, customer-managed keys, CloudTrail trails, IAM users, roles or policies were created. Federated temporary credentials existed only in memory; no access key, secret key or session token is retained.

Kinesis JSON body and HTTP status are preserved for captured calls; HTTP response headers/request IDs were not collected by the shared signing helper. Opaque shard iterators are actual values scoped to the now-deleted stream, not STS credentials.

findings.finding: All five modeled APIs natively support DryRun=true in this account/region: valid requests return HTTP 400 DryRunOperationException, not success status; body has __type and lowercase message with the operation-specific validation-succeeded text. No model/deployment lag was observed for these APIs.

DryRun does not uniformly perform all ordinary semantic validation. GetShardIterator accepts a nonexistent shard and AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER without StartingSequenceNumber, while ordinary controls reject. SubscribeToShard rejects a nonexistent shard but accepts AT_SEQUENCE_NUMBER without SequenceNumber, while its ordinary control rejects.

DryRun GetRecords validates the iterator encoding and StreamARN/name agreement, but a fresh iterator for an already-deleted stream still yields DryRunOperationException even after ordinary GetRecords reports the shard does not exist. A missing StreamARN is accepted when the iterator identifies the stream.

Missing streams/consumers reject PutRecord, PutRecords, GetShardIterator and SubscribeToShard. Sampled model-shape violations reject before resource lookup and before explicit session-policy denial. Malformed ARNs and missing required payloads reject; PutRecord also checks out-of-range ExplicitHashKey.

A real ephemeral STS federation session with explicit denies rejects each valid DryRun operation with HTTP 400 AccessDeniedException and uppercase Message. Denial also precedes missing-resource lookup and GetRecords StreamARN/iterator name-agreement checking in the sampled requests. No persistent IAM resources were created.

The stream was empty when read after dry-run writes. DryRun=false subsequently wrote exactly the two control records; dry-run reading returned only the exception, and ordinary reading with the same iterator returned those two records, with no dry-run sentinel data observed.

The existing consumer description was identical before and after dry-run calls; ListStreamConsumers still showed only the one intentionally registered consumer. Two immediate valid dry-run subscriptions both returned DryRunOperationException. This observes metadata/repeated admission, not proof about live subscription-slot allocation.

Two bounded CloudWatch reads of the same pre-control-write time window returned no IncomingRecords, IncomingBytes, GetRecords.Records or SubscribeToShard.Success datapoints. PutRecord.Success, PutRecords.Success and GetRecords.Success had zero-valued Sum datapoints, so absence of all metric activity is NOT established. The window includes successful dry-run validation, rejected dry-run probes and setup; individual metric emission cannot be attributed to a specific request.
Cleanup confirmed the owned consumer and stream absent, and a complete ListStreams response excluded the owned stream name. The later deleted-stream read probes did not create resources.
